recipes.name: Chicken Fried Rice
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53367. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Fried rice is best made with leftover rice that's at least a day old. Otherwise it becomes gummy in the skillet.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: If you don’t have any leftover rice from the night before, cook a batch of rice and spread it on a large baking sheet or several large plates. Let the rice dry out for about 1 to 2 hours before using it for fried rice.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Rice sticks to the pan very easily, so make sure to use a wok or pan that doesn’t have a sticky surface. I usually cook stir-fries in my seasoned carbon steel wok, but cast iron or nonstick pans work well, too. You might need to add a little more oil if things aren’t releasing easily.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Prepare the chicken:

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Chop the chicken into small 1/4-inch to 1/2-inch cubes. Sprinkle 1/2 teaspoon of salt over the chicken and mix to combine. Set the chicken aside for about 10 minutes (I usually use this time to chop all the vegetables).

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Scramble the egg:

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Heat a wok or large sauté pan over medium-high heat. Swirl in a tablespoon of oil and add the whisked eggs. Use a spatula to quickly scramble the eggs, breaking the curds into smaller pieces as they come together. Transfer the eggs to a plate.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Cook the chicken:

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Add another tablespoon of oil in the wok or pan. Add the chicken and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally. Turn off the heat and transfer the cooked chicken to a plate.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: Using your spatula, scrape off any chicken bits that are still stuck to the wok so they don't burn during the next step. You can also use paper towels to wipe down your wok or pan.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: Cook the vegetables:

steps.title: Step 12
steps.instruction: Swirl 1 tablespoon of oil into the wok over medium-high heat. Add the diced onions and cook them for 1 minute, until they start to soften. Mix in the minced garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the diced carrots and cook for 2 minutes, stirring frequently. Add 1/2 teaspoon salt and the peas, and stir to incorporate.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.instruction: Cook the rice:

steps.title: Step 14
steps.instruction: Add the rice to the wok or pan on top of the vegetables and stir to combine. Using the back of your spatula, smash any large chunks of rice to break them apart. Add the white and green parts of the sliced scallions (save the dark green parts) and five-spice powder. Stir to incorporate. If the rice starts to stick to the pan, stir in a little more oil.

recipes.name: Chinese Orange Chicken
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53365. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Make the orange sauce:

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Whisk together sauce ingredients in a medium bowl. Set aside.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Prep the chicken:

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Cut chicken into about 1-inch cubes. Whisk eggs with salt and black pepper in a bowl and add chicken. Stir together.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: In a separate bowl, whisk together flour and cornstarch. Remove chicken from eggs with a slotted spoon or tongs, letting excess egg drain off, then transfer to cornstarch mixture and coat well.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Fry the chicken:

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Add oil to a large 10- to 12-inch skillet. Heat over medium-high heat until it reaches 350°F. If you don’t have a thermometer, you can also test the temperature by sprinkling in some flour. If the oil is hot enough, it should fizzle immediately.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Once oil is hot, fry the chicken in two batches. The oil might not completely cover the chicken—that’s okay. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes. Flip the chicken pieces and cook until the chicken is cooked through, about 3 to 4 more minutes. Total cook time is about 6 to 8 minutes.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Remove fried chicken cubes and transfer to a plate lined with paper towels, so the chicken can drain. Repeat until all the chicken is cooked.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: Simmer the chicken in the sauce:

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: Once chicken is done, pour out hot oil and wipe pan clean. Add a fresh tablespoon of oil along with chopped garlic and shallot. Cook for a minute and then add the sauce. Simmer the sauce until it starts to thicken.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.instruction: Once the sauce is lightly bubbling, add fried chicken and toss together to coat. The sauce should continue to thicken and stick to the chicken. Let simmer for a minute or two more. Serve orange chicken over cooked white rice, garnished with sesame seeds and fresh scallions.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.instruction: Did you love this recipe? Let us know with a rating and review!

steps.title: Step 14
steps.instruction: LEFTOVERS! The orange chicken keeps well in the fridge for 5 days. Reheat in a skillet with a splash of water over low heat. Freeze the orange chicken for up to 3 months, but be sure to thaw it before reheating so the chicken doesn’t clump together.

recipes.name: Egg Foo Young
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53370. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Make the gravy:

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: In a small saucepan, add the beef stock, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, and white pepper powder over medium heat. Whisk together and bring to a simmer.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Combine the cornstarch and water in a small bowl and whisk to dissolve. Add to the saucepan and whisk until the gravy thickens and coats the back of the spoon, 2 to 3 minutes. Cover the saucepan with a lid and keep it warm on the lowest possible heat.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Make the egg foo young batter:

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: In a medium bowl, whisk together the cornstarch and water until dissolved. Add the eggs, salt, and sugar. Whisk until well combined and there are no more egg white clumps.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Add the green onion, bean sprouts, and shrimp. Stir until everything is evenly coated.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Fry the egg foo young:

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Add the vegetable oil to a large wok; it should reach about 2 inches up the sides. Heat the oil over medium-high heat to 350°F, or until vigorous bubbles form around an inserted wooden chopstick.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: With a ladle, gently and slowly add 1/4 of the omelet batter. Egg foo young should immediately bubble and puff up like magic. Fry until golden brown and crispy on each side, about 2 minutes per side. If there are any light spots, use a ladle to gently baste it with hot oil.

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: Tip

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: Egg foo young can be a bit tricky to flip. The easiest method is to put a tool in each hand (a spider, slotted spoon, tongs, and large chopsticks are all good candidates) and gently coax the omelet over, pulling up on one side and pushing down and around on the other.

steps.title: Step 12
steps.instruction: Remove the omelet and place it on a paper towel-lined baking sheet. Let it cool for 5 minutes. Meanwhile, repeat with the remaining batter to make 4 omelets. If needed, add more oil to the pan between batches.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.instruction: Serve and enjoy:

steps.title: Step 14
steps.instruction: Plate each egg foo young over a bed of rice. Spoon the warm gravy over the top and serve immediately.

recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 52946. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Mix the cornflour and 1 tbsp soy sauce, toss in the prawns and set aside for 10 mins. Stir the vinegar, remaining soy sauce, tomato purée, sugar and 2 tbsp water together to make a sauce.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: When you’re ready to cook, heat a large frying pan or wok until very hot, then add 1 tbsp oil. Fry the prawns until they are golden in places and have opened out– then tip them out of the pan.

steps.instruction: Heat the remaining oil and add the peanuts, chillies and water chestnuts. Stir-fry for 2 mins or until the peanuts start to colour, then add the ginger and garlic and fry for 1 more min. Tip in the prawns and sauce and simmer for 2 mins until thickened slightly. Serve with rice.

recipes.name: Ma Po Tofu
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 52947. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Add a small pinch of salt and sesame oil to minced beef. Mix well and set aside.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Mix 1 tablespoon of cornstarch with 2 and ½ tablespoons of water in a small bowl to make water starch.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Cut tofu into square cubes (around 2cms). Bring a large amount of water to a boil and then add a pinch of salt. Slide the tofu in and cook for 1 minute. Move out and drain.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Get a wok and heat up around 2 tablespoons of oil, fry the minced meat until crispy. Transfer out beef out and leave the oil in.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Fry doubanjiang for 1 minute over slow fire and then add garlic, scallion white, ginger and fermented black beans to cook for 30 seconds until aroma. Then mix pepper flakes in.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Add water to the seasonings and bring to boil over high fire. Gently slide the tofu cubes. Add light soy sauce and beef.Slow the heat after boiling and then simmer for 6-8 minutes. Then add chopped garlic greens.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Stir the water starch and then pour half of the mixture to the simmering pot. Wait for around 30 seconds and then pour the other half. You can slightly taste the tofu and add pinch of salt if not salty enough. By the way, if you feel it is too spicy, add some sugar can milder the taste. But be carefully as the broth is very hot at this point.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Transfer out when almost all the seasonings stick to tofu cubes. Sprinkle Szechuan peppercorn powder (to taste)and chopped garlic greens if using.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Serve immediately with steamed rice.

steps.instruction: Dried shrimp gives this Chinese dish a punch of salty umami flavor. You can find it at an Asian grocery store in the frozen or refrigerated section. Look for small-sized dried shrimp, about a 1/4-inch in size. If you use medium or large dried shrimp, hydrate the shrimp with more water (1 cup for medium-sized shrimp, 1 1/4 cup for large) and for longer time (45 to 60 minutes), then chop it up into smaller 1/4-inch chunks. To make this recipe vegetarian, omit the dried shrimp and use four or five dried shiitake mushrooms, rehydrated, and sliced thin.

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: This recipe calls for asian eggplants, or Japanese eggplants. They are long and thin compared to a European or globe eggplant, and much more tender and delicate. If you can't find them you can substitute globe eggplant, but the dish is really best with the asian eggplant.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: *A lot of grocery stores have Asian ingredient aisles now. You should be able to find chili-bean paste, a mixture of preserved chilies mixed with mashed soybeans, there or at any Asian market. (Do not confuse with black bean paste or chili-garlic paste.)

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: **Sichuan peppercorns are available at some stores and online for quite cheap. They aren't spicy like other peppers but rather have a citrusy flavor and induce a tingly, numbing sensation like a carbonated drink.

steps.title: Step 4

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: For the sweet onion, look for Vidalia, OSO Sweet, or Walla Walla. The super-sweet varieties are more suited to this stir-fry because at the end of cooking, the onion still has a slight crunch.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Make the sauce:

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: In a bowl, combine the sesame oil, soy sauce, and rice vinegar.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Cook the rice noodles:

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Bring a large saucepan of water to a boil, add the noodles, and use tongs to turn them so they are submerged. Cook for 2 minutes, or until they are tender but still have some bite (they will cook a little more once you add them to the skillet).

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Drain, rinse with cold water, and use scissors to snip the noodles several times to break them up into shorter lengths.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Scramble the eggs:

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: In a small bowl whisk together the eggs. Heat the skillet or Dutch oven over medium heat. Add 1 tablespoon of the peanut or canola oil. Add the eggs and scramble them for 2 minutes, or until they form large, soft curds. Transfer them from the pan to a plate or bowl.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Cook the vegetables:

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: Add 1 tablespoon of the remaining oil to the pan. When it is hot, add the ginger, garlic, carrots, jalapeño, onion, and salt. Cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes or until the vegetables start to soften.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: Add the remaining ingredients:

steps.title: Step 12
steps.instruction: Sprinkle the vegetable mixture with the remaining 1 tablespoon peanut or canola oil. When the oil is hot, add the ham, cabbage, scallions, red pepper, and curry powder to the pan. Cook, stirring constantly, for 1 minute.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.instruction: Add the shrimp and cook, stirring, for 3 more minutes or until the shrimp are bright pink and cooked through.

recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Chicken
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 53376. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Coat the chicken with egg white:

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: In a bowl, combine the chicken with the egg white, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and cornstarch. Stir to coat the chicken evenly. Let sit for 15 minutes at room temperature or up to overnight in the refrigerator.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Make the sweet and sour sauce:

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Whisk together the pineapple juice, vinegar, ketchup, 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt, and brown sugar.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Stir-fry the chicken over high heat:

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Heat a large frying pan or wok over high heat until a bead of water instantly sizzles and evaporates. Pour in 1 tablespoon of cooking oil and swirl to coat. It's important that the pan is very hot.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Add the chicken and spread the pieces out in one layer. Let the chicken fry untouched for 1 minute, until the bottoms are browned.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Flip and fry the other side for 1 minute. The chicken should still be pinkish in the middle. Dish out the chicken onto a clean plate, leaving as much oil in the pan as possible.

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Stir-fry the bell pepper and ginger:

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: Reduce the heat to medium and add the remaining 1 teaspoon of cooking oil. Let the oil heat up before adding the bell pepper chunks and ginger. Fry for 1 minute.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: Add the pineapple, sauce, and then, the chicken:

steps.title: Step 12
steps.instruction: Add the pineapple chunks and the sweet and sour sauce. Turn up the heat to high. When the sauce is simmering, add the chicken pieces back in.

steps.title: Step 13
steps.instruction: Let simmer for 1 to 2 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through. Timing depends on how thick you've cut your chicken. The best way to tell if the chicken is done is to take a piece out and cut into it. If it's pink, add another minute to the cooking.

steps.title: Step 14
steps.instruction: Adjust the seasoning and serve:

steps.title: Step 1

steps.instruction: 2. Slice the pork tenderloin into strips.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: 3. Prepare the marinade using a pinch of salt, one teaspoon of starch, two teaspoons of light soy sauce, and an egg white.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: 4. Marinade the pork strips for about 20 minutes.

steps.title: Step 7

steps.title: Step 9
steps.instruction: Cooking Instructions

steps.title: Step 10
steps.instruction: 1. Pour the cooking oil into a wok and heat to 190°C (375°F). Add the marinated pork strips and fry them until they turn brown. Remove the cooked pork from the wok and place on a plate.

steps.title: Step 11
steps.instruction: 2. Leave some oil in the wok. Put the tomato sauce and white sugar into the wok, and heat until the oil and sauce are fully combined.

steps.title: Step 12

steps.instruction: 4. Pour in the starchy sauce. Stir-fry all the ingredients until the pork and sauce are thoroughly mixed together.

recipes.name: Wontons
recipes.notes: Source: TheMealDB id 52948. Free for commercial use. https://www.themealdb.com/

steps.title: Step 1
steps.instruction: Combine pork, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, sesame oil, and vegetables in a bowl.

steps.title: Step 2
steps.instruction: Separate wonton skins.

steps.title: Step 3
steps.instruction: Place a heaping teaspoon of filling in the center of the wonton.

steps.title: Step 4
steps.instruction: Brush water on 2 borders of the skin, covering 1/4 inch from the edge.

steps.title: Step 5
steps.instruction: Fold skin over to form a triangle, sealing edges.

steps.title: Step 6
steps.instruction: Pinch the two long outside points together.

steps.title: Step 7
steps.instruction: Heat oil to 450 degrees and fry 4 to 5 at a time until golden.

steps.title: Step 8
steps.instruction: Drain and serve with sauce.
